remediated.cause: Legacy slug collision suppressed the real squad task; explicit canonical task field now pins owner-verified squad target.
Legacy slug found SQL EXPLAIN core task; explicit canonical task field now pins owner-verified content analytics target.

method: Compare canonical responsibility, exact task owner, real input and output. Resolver/file existence alone is insufficient; no positional or title mapping.

consultation.result: No additional semantic blocker; automated QA does not prove WCAG, assistive technology, physical devices or reduced-motion information equivalence.

contracts.name: Capacity-aware Reel/carousel editorial calendar
contracts.input: Approved pillars, seasonal dates, Reel/carousel platforms, real production capacity and measurement definitions.
contracts.output: Dated slots with pillar/funnel/theme, owners, production lead time, flex capacity and tracking.
contracts.rationale: North plans editorial distribution; task example cadences are choices to validate, not universal posting requirements.

criteria.check: Map slots to supplied pillars, audience/funnel and dated events; label unsupported themes and timing assumptions.
Fit deadlines, dependencies, review and flex slots to actual capacity without inventing approvals or reach.
Define tracking window/unit and owners; a calendar plans production and authorizes no automatic posting.

negative.input: Daily Reels planned despite one weekly production slot and unverified holiday date.
negative.expected: Reject capacity/date conflict; reduce or defer slots and preserve explicit review before publication.

contracts.name: Source-bound Reel/carousel performance analysis
contracts.input: Actual platform metrics, content IDs, KPI definitions, time window, denominators and comparable history.
contracts.output: Metric/source table, KPI comparisons, grounded patterns, uncertainty and next-cycle test recommendations.
contracts.rationale: Lens analyses editorial metrics; SQL query optimisation is another domain and correlation does not establish format causality.

criteria.check: Pin source, content IDs, window, unit, denominator and deduplication before comparing platform metrics.
Compare like populations/windows and expose missing data; distinguish correlation and selection bias from causality.
Tie recommendations to observed patterns and bounded tests; no invented ROI, causal gain or reserved experiment result.

negative.input: Five high-spend Reels vs unpaid carousels; raw impressions used to claim threefold causal format gain.
negative.expected: Reject causal comparison; separate spend/population/denominator and propose controlled follow-up.

contracts.name: Scoped accessibility audit and remediation
contracts.input: Implemented pages/components, declared flows, WCAG target and test environment.
contracts.output: Criterion matrix, findings, remediation owners and scoped verdict.
contracts.rationale: Aperture audits and prescribes; implementation remains Scaffold's responsibility.

criteria.check: List criterion ID, level, applicability and source/version; no blanket count or legal compliance claim.
Observe keyboard/focus/reflow and real assistive technology; mark unavailable checks unverified.
Block critical failures; automated score cannot replace missing manual evidence or authorize publish.

negative.input: Axe passes but dialog traps focus and no screen-reader run exists.
negative.expected: FAIL for trap; AT unverified; no complete compliance verdict.

contracts.name: Token taxonomy and consumer contract
contracts.input: Approved brand tokens, visual specs, existing token consumers and theme requirements.
contracts.output: Versioned taxonomy, names, reference rules and handoff; implementation deferred.
contracts.rationale: Lattice governs token/API architecture, not visual decisions or component implementation.

criteria.check: Resolve declared primitive/semantic/component references without cycles, dangling names or ambiguous types.
Document names, theme overrides, exports and breaking-change impact on actual consumers.
Preserve approved brand values and existing consumers; no automatic migration or implementation claim.

negative.input: Component token points at a missing semantic token in dark mode.
negative.expected: Reject the reference chain and expose affected consumers before handoff.

contracts.name: Component interaction and interruption specification
contracts.input: Visual states, motion tokens, triggers, product purpose and accessibility constraints.
contracts.output: State/trigger spec, timings, interruption behavior, reduced alternative and implementer handoff.
contracts.rationale: Gesture specifies product motion; brand motion and formal accessibility review remain separate.

criteria.check: Define trigger, state change, feedback, timing units and final state for each included component.
Specify interruption, repeated activation and reduced-motion path preserving information and focus.
Document implementation handoff and measured-budget acceptance; spec or transform choice alone proves no FPS.

negative.input: Modal dismissed halfway through entrance; reduce preference changes at runtime.
negative.expected: Deterministic closed state and returned focus; essential status retained without decorative motion.

contracts.name: Reproducible web performance diagnosis
contracts.input: Exact URL/build, user interactions, device/network targets, budgets and field data if available.
contracts.output: Per-URL measured results, bottleneck evidence, remediation owners and limits.
contracts.rationale: Velocity measures and prescribes; lab fixture and aggregate score do not establish field p75.

criteria.check: Pin URL/build, device, network, interactions and repeated measurement conditions.
Separate lab observations from real field distributions; mark unavailable INP/field evidence unverified.
Tie bottlenecks and proposed fixes to traces; certify only declared measured scope, never publish by score.

negative.input: Single Lighthouse run, no user interaction or field data, label says all users meet INP p75.
negative.expected: Reject certification; report lab-only evidence and missing field/interaction data.

contracts.name: Responsive screen composition and handoff
contracts.input: Wireframe brief, approved copy, brand/DS tokens, content hierarchy and responsive constraints.
contracts.output: Screen designs, visual states, grid/reflow notes and implementation handoff.
contracts.rationale: Palette composes UI; does not invent brand foundations or claim implemented behavior.

criteria.check: Trace hierarchy, grouping, typography and spacing to task and approved brand tokens.
Review desktop and 390px reflow, content order, long text and included empty/error/focus states.
Specify states and responsive rules without overflow or hidden essential content; design is not runtime proof.

negative.input: Long project title and empty/error states at 390px with desktop-only sidebar.
negative.expected: Expose overflow/content loss; adapt hierarchy and provide explicit state/reflow rules.

contracts.name: Structural wireframe brief grounded in user flow
contracts.input: IA, user flows, evidence-backed scenarios, content hierarchy and business constraints.
contracts.output: Structural briefs by template, annotations, assumptions, responsive notes and UI handoff.
contracts.rationale: Vantage defines structure/brief; task wording mentioning detailed wireframes does not expand role into visual design.

criteria.check: Trace scenario, user need and priority to supplied research; label unsupported personas/assumptions.
Map template regions, content slots, action/results, reflow and failure recovery to the supplied IA.
Keep visual/token/code decisions delegated; no invented research or usability validation result.

negative.input: Brief requires account recovery but available flow omits failure/back navigation; no persona research.
negative.expected: Expose flow gap and persona assumption; no invented test success or visual implementation.

contracts.name: Design pipeline assignments and gate receipts
contracts.input: Selected workflow, DX brief, assets, authority, dependencies and specialist status.
contracts.output: Assignments, verified handoffs, scoped gate receipts and unresolved blockers.
contracts.rationale: Nexus coordinates specialists; canonical output calling a pipeline successful is contingent on actual receipts.

criteria.check: Assign real specialists/tasks by role with input/output dependencies, ownership and bounded loops.
Require observed accessibility/performance receipts; absent or failed gates block delivery progression.
Orchestrator creates no domain code/design and no unapproved publish; preserve concurrent work.

negative.input: UI complete but keyboard gate failed and performance evidence absent.
negative.expected: Block progression, delegate remediation and report the missing receipts.

contracts.name: Motion intent and execution brief
contracts.input: Raw request, extracted intent, surface/brand context, device constraints and authorized references.
contracts.output: Purpose, from/to parameters, triggers, fallback, assets and actual executor/task.
contracts.rationale: Decoder interprets into a brief and delegates implementation; subjective adjectives are assumptions to test.

criteria.check: Distinguish observed request/reference from inference; connect motion to purpose and target surface.
Declare states, timing units, triggers, interruptions and reduced alternative preserving information.
Resolve chosen task/executor, asset rights and declared budget; unavailable inputs remain blockers.

negative.input: Request says elegant but gives no assets/device; proposed shader has unknown license and no fallback.
negative.expected: Mark inferences and missing rights; constrain or defer implementation without claiming observed reference.

contracts.name: Timing and reduced-motion specification
contracts.input: Animation brief, element list, interaction frequency and perception/accessibility constraints.
contracts.output: Per-element durations/easing/delays, sequence bounds and alternative timing.
contracts.rationale: Tempo specifies choreography; source duration tables are starting hypotheses rather than universal rules.

criteria.check: Declare units, starts/ends, easing and total duration consistently with the interaction purpose.
Specify repeated activation/interruption and reduced path; avoid delaying essential focus or status.
Distinguish designed timing from observed rhythm; independent playback review is required for perception.

negative.input: Ten elements stagger indefinitely; final CTA delayed and focus invisible until animation ends.
negative.expected: Reject timing/control conflict; essential focus immediate and bounded sequence with reduced alternative.

contracts.name: Scroll motion with scoped lifecycle and fallback
contracts.input: Scroll spec, real layout, selected stack, device/input targets and ownership boundary.
contracts.output: Configured animation, native/reduced fallback, teardown and reproducible interaction evidence.
contracts.rationale: Parallax implements scroll behavior; universal getAll().kill() snippets must not destroy other owners' triggers.

criteria.check: Preserve native wheel/touch/keyboard control and essential content without JS or reduced motion.
One owned clock/scroll integration; repeated setup/teardown removes only owned triggers/listeners/resources.
Measure declared target and layout/reflow effects; emulation or composited properties prove no physical FPS.

negative.input: Another feature owns a ScrollTrigger; current animation unmounts during scroll.
negative.expected: Only current owner cleaned; foreign trigger survives and content remains reachable.

contracts.name: Shader code, uniforms and fallback
contracts.input: Effect specification, configured scene, uniform ranges, texture rights and actual GPU target.
contracts.output: Compiled shader/interface, bounded parameters, scoped lifecycle and unsupported-context fallback.
contracts.rationale: Fragment owns shader effects; scene setup and independent target performance remain delegated.

criteria.check: Compile on declared context, capture diagnostics and document uniform types/ranges, resolution and color assumptions.
Context loss/unsupported GPU/reduced motion preserves essential content with bounded fallback.
Dispose only owned resources/listeners; measure actual target before FPS or universal precision claims.

negative.input: Shader fails compile or WebGL context is lost while shared texture belongs to another feature.
negative.expected: Readable fallback; diagnostic exposed; shared texture not disposed.

contracts.name: Bounded particle emitter and lifecycle
contracts.input: Particle brief, finite count/memory budget, seed/data rights, scene and target devices.
contracts.output: Emitter/forces, bounded pooling, pause/reduced behavior, teardown and target evidence.
contracts.rationale: Cloud owns generative system; source count tables and million-particle statements cannot establish observed capacity.

criteria.check: Finite validated limits, reproducible seed and spawn/recycle invariants prevent unbounded growth or invalid values.
Choose rendering by measured target budget; pause/reduced fallback preserves information, no universal scale/FPS claim.
Repeated lifecycle releases owned geometry/material/FBO/listeners and preserves borrowed scene resources.

negative.input: Emitter receives infinite rate/negative lifetime, then remounts with a borrowed texture.
negative.expected: Reject invalid input; bounded pool and owned teardown leave shared resources intact.

contracts.name: Animation assignments, dependencies and review gates
contracts.input: Executable animation brief, authorized assets, target context and specialist availability.
contracts.output: Real executor/task assignments, bounded dependencies, gate receipts and blockers.
contracts.rationale: Kinetic coordinates implementation and review; award-quality language is not an observed result.

criteria.check: Resolve each executor/task from actual role and dependency; vague requests go to interpreter first.
Observe declared visual/technical/accessibility/performance scope; missing playback/device proof stays unverified.
Bound independent assignments and iterations; orchestrator writes no domain animation code and authorizes no publish.

negative.input: Shader target device absent, only sampled frames, proposed final cinematic PASS.
negative.expected: Report unavailable continuous/device review, delegate remaining gates and block unsupported final claim.

contracts.name: Versioned content template and validation rules
contracts.input: Approved carousel/Reel template, platform, fields, visual assets and dated technical specifications.
contracts.output: Versioned contract with field/slide bounds, required assets, hard gates and validator handoff.
contracts.rationale: Morph formalizes template constraints; registration does not prove enforcement or published content.

criteria.check: Declare unique ID/version, required fields, count and character bounds, order, dimensions and assets.
Pin source/date of platform limits and rights; distinguish supplied brief choices from universal platform rules.
Define hard/soft failures and test missing/overflow fields before claiming enforcement or allowing handoff.

negative.input: Carousel contains an extra slide, missing mandatory proof field and stale platform specs.
negative.expected: Hard fail required/count violations; expose stale-spec gap without automatic publication.

contracts.name: Reel script adaptation and platform contract
contracts.input: Approved script/message, versioned Reel contract, licensed assets/audio and current platform evidence.
contracts.output: Adapted script, overlay/caption plan, format/audio choices and governor handoff.
contracts.rationale: Morph adapts a supplied script; task recommendations about trending audio and retention are hypotheses, not algorithm guarantees.

criteria.check: Match declared format/duration/field limits and device safe zones to the dated template and supplied brief.
Preserve factual message and mute comprehension; caption timing/contrast and audio rights remain traceable.
No promised reach/retention from trend choice; adaptation is not render, heard-audio review or publish approval.

negative.input: Trending track lacks reuse rights and key instruction exists only in audio.
negative.expected: Reject unauthorized track and add equivalent readable information; distribution gain remains unproven.

contracts.name: Content quality findings and protected gates
contracts.input: Finished carousel/Reel, brief, template version, claims/assets provenance and observed review channels.
contracts.output: Criterion findings, protected pass/fail, correction handoff and unobserved-media limits.
contracts.rationale: Index audits, does not create or publish; numeric average cannot override template, factual or rights failures.

criteria.check: Trace message, proof, direction and originality to brief and attributable sources; invented proof is blocked.
Required fields, asset rights and factual accuracy fail independently of average quality score.
Review readable artifact and available channels; unheard audio/unseen continuity prevents audiovisual total or publish approval.

negative.input: Average score is nine but testimonial is invented and audio was never heard.
negative.expected: FAIL unsupported proof; audiovisual review incomplete; no automatic publication.

contracts.name: Source-grounded signal brief for Reel/carousel
contracts.input: Dated daily signal logs, source locators, pillar/funnel constraints and available formats.
contracts.output: Deduplicated priorities, evidence, uncertainty and suggested format/template handoff.
contracts.rationale: Radar curates signals for production; viral scores are estimates and do not establish audience performance.

criteria.check: Keep source locator/date, observed signal and duplicate lineage; separate claim from inference.
Map each chosen signal to declared pillar/audience and Reel/carousel purpose; unsupported fit stays explicit.
Mark priority/viral potential as hypothesis; unavailable sources and rights cannot become fabricated proof.

negative.input: Three reposts repeat one stale claim; no original source or fit to current pillar.
negative.expected: One uncertain lineage, no independent corroboration claim; defer or reject editorial recommendation.

contracts.name: Content assignments, versioned handoffs and QA state
contracts.input: Editorial plan/signals, current work status, capacity, template versions and brand assets.
contracts.output: Owned assignments, dependency/status records, QA receipts and unresolved blockers.
contracts.rationale: Bulletin coordinates specialists; workflow publication stage does not grant external sending authority.

criteria.check: Assign real tasks with required inputs, template version, owner/capacity and bounded dependencies.
Record observed production/QA status; missing assets or protected failures block subsequent phases.
Orchestrator creates no domain content; no publish/send or automatic global learning from project feedback.

negative.input: Carousel enters publication queue with failed rights gate and client-local preference.
negative.expected: Blocked publication status; correction assigned and preference stays local/candidate.

contracts.name: Editable SVG icon set and integration guide
contracts.input: Approved guidelines/palette, existing icon inventory, permitted new assets and usage sizes.
contracts.output: Editable SVGs/sprite, fallbacks, semantic-use guide and small-size visual evidence.
contracts.rationale: Ember creates code-based brand assets; a source nickname mismatch does not change canonical agent identity.

criteria.check: Validate SVG/viewBox/symbol IDs, consistent stroke/style and legibility at requested small sizes.
Use approved brand primitives and attributable asset rights; document accessible/decorative integration semantics.
Preserve functioning inventory; reject unsafe active SVG/external resources and verify sprite references.
criteria.method: Unsafe SVG and broken-symbol negative case

negative.input: Icon includes script/external fetch or duplicate symbol ID and obscures status at 16px.
negative.expected: Reject unsafe/colliding asset and require legible status plus integration guidance.

contracts.name: Editable video template and sync handoff
contracts.input: Approved motion/visual/sonic identity, Reel brief, duration, rights and available export tools.
contracts.output: Requested editable templates, format manifest, timeline/sync points and missing-tool gaps.
contracts.rationale: Ripple creates reusable branded graphics; fixed intro lengths, export claims and 50ms offsets require context and observation.

criteria.check: Map requested template blocks/exports to editable files and declared duration; unavailable formats remain gaps.
Document actual visual/audio cues and review complete playback when perceptually available; no universal sync offset.
Preserve brand/rights, caption safe areas and readable timing; sampled frames alone prove no audiovisual PASS.

negative.input: Only MP4 exists but manifest claims editable AE/CSS/Lottie and perfectly heard sync.
negative.expected: Reject export/observation claims; report actual files, missing editable formats and unobserved audio.

contracts.name: Audio bed masters, rights and listening review
contracts.input: Sonic identity, Reel context/duration, voice mix, authorized sound sources and output formats.
contracts.output: Actual masters/variants, rights manifest, mix metrics and available listening/device evidence.
contracts.rationale: Echo designs audio beds; codec/RMS/LUFS and music theory tags cannot prove heard quality, seamlessness or voice clarity.

criteria.check: Trace sound/source rights, authored scope and actual duration/format variants; no unmade collection claim.
Measure declared mix/codec/clipping and loop boundaries; numerical levels alone do not establish audibility.
Listen to full bed and voice/device context before seamlessness, intelligibility or artistic PASS; unavailable listening stays unverified.

negative.input: Decoded waveform is valid but no listening occurred; voice is masked or boundary clicks.
negative.expected: Technical-only result, audible quality unverified/failed when heard; no total audiovisual score.

rejected.reason: Mission references squads/design/tasks; exact command does not resolve and no compatible real task is declared. Legacy contracts remain candidates.
Mission router references development task that does not resolve for this agent; no invented pointer or persona-derived expertise.
Canonical responsibilities exist but no real exact primary task resolves; dark-pattern/performance assertions do not become contracts.
Canonical command exists but corresponding executable task is absent/unresolved; canon title alone is not a binding.
Canonical command exists but exact task is absent/unresolved; premium aesthetics do not establish pricing or conversion.
Canonical command exists but exact task is absent/unresolved; product surface responsibilities remain candidates.

limits: Semantic review defines bounded principal contracts, not full-role expertise or completed source acquisition.
Original seven profiles/eighteen bindings preserved; no candidate source promoted to READ.
Negative cases are evaluation requirements, not observed held-out artifact results.
Unsupported domain claims in canonical task prose remain visible as gaps; protected files are unchanged.
Only current UI/motion, Reel and carousel families are added; no advertising/other family expansion.

validation.regression: All-agent suite caught core/squad-creator legacy task syntax; explicit command task extension restricted to domain squads. Corrected and all 172 resolve without changing core source.
